dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Anita. How can I help you?

Hi, yeah, good afternoon. I'm calling for my mother, she's at 277 Farewell Street, up the North End. She wants to put in a fence, you know, and I'm trying to figure out what she needs. I mean, does a fence even need a permit? Right?
Generally, yes, a fence often does need a permit here, but it depends on the height and where it goes. Tell me what she's planning.

Okay, so, it's for the vegetable garden in the back. The deer keep coming in and eating everything, you know, and after the soaker Wednesday and Thursday, yesterday, the whole yard's a mess anyway, so she wants to get ahead of it. I mean, she wants a white picket style. About four and a half feet tall.
Okay, four and a half feet, picket style. Is it only around the garden, or along the property line?
Um, just around the garden, I think. Not the property line. Is that different? I don't, I mean, I don't really get how that works.
It can be different, yes. Distance from the lot line matters, so I'd have someone from the office look at the plan. You'd want to submit a simple sketch showing where it sits on the lot.

A sketch, okay. And, so, if she hires a contractor, does the contractor pull the permit, or is that on her, the owner? Because I thought the contractor did it, but my cousin says the owner does. Right?
Either can work. A contractor can apply on her behalf, but the permit is for her property, so she should confirm who's doing it before work starts. Make sure it's in writing.
Okay, so, either one. Got it. Wait, so who, the contractor or her, ends up responsible if it's wrong?
The owner ultimately, since it's her property. That's why I'd confirm it up front.
Okay. Um, one more. The finished side, the nice side, does that have to face out? Toward the neighbors, or the street? You know, I heard that's a rule.
That's a common requirement, finished side facing out, but I'd have the inspector confirm it for her setup. I can take your number and have someone call you back.
Sure, yeah, it's 401-555-0175. Nelson Correia. I'm driving over to her place later, out past Island Park in Portsmouth, it's wicked quiet down there this time of year, so I'll tell her all this.
Got it, Nelson, 401-555-0175. Someone will call you back. Have a good weekend.
Okay, thanks. So, just to be sure, permit probably yes, sketch, and finished side out, right? Okay. Thanks.
